problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=⟨\frac{1}{3-t},\,\sqrt{t+2},\,{e}^{2t}⟩.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Domain of a Vector-Valued Function

feedback.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-4}\,i+t\,j+\sqrt{t-2}\,k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-4}$ is $t\in (-\infty -2)\cup (-2,2)\cup (2,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\sqrt{t-2}$ is $t\in [2,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14076578/assets/18bd3e410f2f3e415e8164ae6e2f9e03a2f7281ce15e6e05cb570ecfdac10964.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in (2,\infty ).$
